newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Prices, credit main problems in Brazil coffee sale.
newsitem.headline: Prices, credit main problems in Brazil coffee sale.

text.p: Unattractive prices and difficulty in obtaining credit from Banco do Brasil were the main reasons for a low level of sales in the Brazilian government's monthly coffee auction, said a roaster official.
"There were two main problems - prices and credit," said David Nahum, secretary-general of the Brazilian Coffee Industry Association (ABIC) which represents roasters.

Of the 326,188 60-kg bags offered, only 128,660 or 39.44 percent were sold. Of the 300,273 bags on offer to exporters, the domestic roasting and the soluble industry, sales totalled only 102,745 bags.
The remaining 25,915 bags were made available only to the soluble industry, all of which were sold.

Nahum said that apart from the actual prices asked in the auction, buyers had to face higher transport costs and expenses to remove the coffee from warehouses than if they were buying in the domestic market.
Also credit lines with Banco do Brasil were becoming increasingly more difficult to obtain, he added.
"The problems had already started in the last auction but this one was even more difficult," Nahum said.
